findings.title: Prove the observed waiter blocks before dependency expiry
findings.description: The required expiry-crossing oracle is not established. trusted_before_wait is observed at lines 2046-2047 before creating the blocker connection and launching the worker. observe_blocked (1044-1054) returns only pid, blocking pids and query; neither it nor the caller asserts a trusted time below the immutable admission_end when the actual worker is blocked. If connection setup or scheduling delays the worker beyond the remaining 0.5-second interval, it can reach the lock after expiry, be observed blocked, then deny and leave zero effects while this test still passes. The original four raw records and the independent four records have no blocked-at trusted timestamp, so they cannot distinguish that false-positive ordering from expiry crossed during a lock wait. The actual merged guard uses fresh post-lock clock_timestamp, but this regression oracle would not reliably prove that requirement.
findings.requested_action: In this task-owned test, capture a trusted database clock alongside observation of the real blocking waiter and assert that blocked_at precedes the original immutable source_end before crossing the bound and releasing the blocker. Preserve the four T6/START/CONTINUE/RESUME exact denial and unchanged-inventory assertions, bounded waits, and absence of caller clocks/timestamp overwrites. Regenerate every required task check on the new implementation SHA and obtain fresh independent reviews.
